entities.summary: John II of Baden was a titular Margrave of Baden and Archbishop and Elector of Trier from 1456 until his death in 1503. He played a key role in the politics of Western Europe during the Late Middle Ages. Born into a powerful noble family, John II of Baden was chosen as Archbishop of Trier at the age of 32, a position he held until his death in 1503. His tenure as Archbishop was marked by a series of conflicts with neighboring states and the Holy Roman Emperor, but he also oversaw significant architectural and artistic projects in the city of Trier. John II of Baden's legacy as a leader of the Catholic Church in Western Europe was cemented by his appointment as Archbishop-Elector of Trier, a position that made him a key player in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire. Despite his influence, John II of Baden's life was marked by controversy and power struggles, as he navigated the treacherous waters of medieval politics to secure his place as a leading figure in Western Europe. His reign as Archbishop and Elector of Trier came to an end with his death in 1503, but his impact on the region's history continued to be felt for centuries to come.
